competitions.solution_summary: Ensemble of LightGBM and LSTM with 'Airport-State' encoding. 1st place utilized a LightGBM model to capture tabular features like flight type and an LSTM to model the current queue of aircraft at the airport. They implemented a 'Congestion-Index' feature that measured the number of active ground moves per hour, which was the single most predictive signal.

competitions.title: Google Earth Engine - Global Wildfire Severity 2026
competitions.evaluation_metric: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) on Burn Severity
competitions.prompt: Predict the burn severity of active wildfires to prioritize disaster response resources. Data: Sentinel-2 post-fire imagery and multi-temporal moisture levels. Goal: Predict the 'Difference Normalized Burn Ratio' (dNBR). Challenge: Differentiating between high-severity fire and natural forest gaps in dense canopy areas.
competitions.solution_summary: Multi-modal U-Net with Residual-Attention. 1st place utilized a U-Net architecture that fused RGB, NIR, and SWIR (Short-Wave Infrared) bands. They implemented a 'Residual-Attention' block that helped the model focus on the drastic spectral changes between pre-fire and post-fire observations. They used 'Pseudo-labeling' from high-resolution drone surveys to refine the masks.

competitions.title: Google Landmark Recognition 2025 - Global Search
competitions.prompt: Identify world landmarks in images across 100,000+ classes from around the globe. Data: 3M images with high label noise and varied viewing angles. Goal: Predict landmark ID. Challenge: Extreme 'fine-grained' architectural differences between similar-style buildings across different cities.
competitions.solution_summary: Sub-center ArcFace with Global and Local Descriptors. 1st place utilized an ensemble of ConvNeXt-XL and DeiT-Large models. They implemented 'Sub-center ArcFace' to handle intra-class visual diversity (e.g., inside vs outside of a museum) and utilized 'Local Feature Re-ranking' using DELF to confirm the most ambiguous predictions.

competitions.title: Google ASL Fingerspelling 2024
competitions.prompt: Translate fingerspelled American Sign Language from mobile video frames into text. Data: Hand-landmark sequences (x, y, z) from MediaPipe. Goal: Predict the character string. Challenge: Extremely high-speed signing (>5 characters per second) where individual frames are highly blurred.
competitions.solution_summary: Squeeze-and-Excitation Transformer with CTC Loss. 1st place utilized a 12-layer Transformer encoder with 'Squeeze-and-Excitation' blocks to weight landmark importance. They implemented 'CTC Loss' (Connectionist Temporal Classification) to handle the alignment between signing frames and characters. They used 'Temporal-Drop' to make the model robust to dropped video frames.

competitions.title: Foursquare - Location Matching
competitions.prompt: Match different listings for the same business/location from multiple sources. Data: Listing names, addresses, and GPS coordinates. Goal: Predict which pairs of IDs represent the same place. Challenge: Non-standard naming (e.g., 'Starbucks' vs 'Starbucks Coffee') and noisy, approximate GPS coordinates.
competitions.solution_summary: Two-stage Retrieval and GBDT Ranking. 1st place used 'K-Nearest Neighbors' (KNN) on GPS coordinates to find the top 50 candidates for each listing. In the second stage, they used an XGBoost model to rank these candidates using string-similarity features (Levenshtein, Jaccard) and geographic distance. They used 'Cross-feature interactions' like 'Name-match AND Distance < 10m'.

competitions.title: Shopee - Price Match Guarantee
competitions.prompt: Identify duplicate product listings across different sellers based on images and titles. Data: Images, product titles, and seller info. Goal: Predict all IDs that match a given product. Challenge: Visually similar products with different packaging and titles in multiple languages.
competitions.solution_summary: Multimodal Metric Learning with ArcFace. 1st place utilized an ensemble of EfficientNet-B3 (for images) and RoBERTa-Base (for titles). They mapped both images and text into a shared 512-dimensional embedding space using ArcFace loss. They utilized 'Nearest-Neighbor' search with a specific threshold to find clusters of identical products.

competitions.title: Eedi - Mining Misconceptions in Mathematics
competitions.prompt: Identify the specific mathematical misconception a student holds based on their wrong answer to a diagnostic question. Data: Math questions, the student's incorrect choice, and a list of 2,000+ known misconceptions. Goal: Predict the correct misconception ID. Challenge: Understanding the 'logic' behind a wrong answer across varied math topics.
competitions.solution_summary: Cross-Encoder retrieval using DeBERTa-v3-Large. 1st place utilized a two-stage approach: a Bi-Encoder first retrieved the top 100 candidate misconceptions, followed by a DeBERTa-v3-Large Cross-Encoder that ranked the candidates by reasoning through the question text. They utilized 'Chain-of-Thought' augmentation during training to help the model learn the steps of wrong-answer logic.

competitions.title: Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2021
competitions.prompt: Improve smartphone GPS accuracy by processing raw GNSS measurements. Data: Raw pseudorange and carrier-phase logs from smartphones. Goal: Predict latitude/longitude. Challenge: Correcting for massive multipath noise and 'cycle slips' in urban canyons.
competitions.solution_summary: EKF with Carrier-Phase smoothing and RTS Backward filtering. 1st place utilized an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that combined pseudorange with 'Phase-Difference' measurements. They implemented a 'Rauch-Tung-Striebel' (RTS) backward smoother to refine the entire trajectory. They used road-snapping via a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to improve suburban driving accuracy.

competitions.title: Google Landmark Retrieval 2018
competitions.prompt: Find matching images for a query landmark image from a database of 1M+ photos. Data: Query photos and an index set. Goal: Return a ranked list of relevant images. Challenge: Handling 'distractor' images and achieving high retrieval speed while maintaining precision for rare landmarks.
competitions.solution_summary: Global descriptor retrieval with DELF re-ranking. 1st place utilized an ensemble of ResNet-101 models to extract global descriptors. They implemented 'Query Expansion' (QE) and 'Database Augmentation' (DBA) to improve the initial retrieval set. They used 'DELF' (Deep Local Features) for geometric verification of the top candidates using RANSAC.

competitions.title: Google ASL Fingerspelling 2026 - Edge Edition
competitions.prompt: Optimize ASL fingerspelling translation for low-power mobile devices. Data: Hand-landmark sequences from mobile cameras. Goal: Predict the character string. Challenge: Achieving high accuracy with a model small enough to run in real-time (<50ms latency) on an entry-level smartphone.
competitions.solution_summary: Knowledge Distillation from a Large Transformer to a Tiny SqueezeNet. 1st place utilized a 'Teacher-Student' framework where a large 24-layer Transformer taught a 4-layer MobileNet-v3 based student. They implemented 'Quantization-Aware Training' (QAT) to compress the model to 8-bit integers without losing accuracy on fast-signing sequences.

competitions.title: Google Landmark Retrieval 2022
competitions.prompt: Find matching landmark images in a massive index given a query image. Data: 1M+ images. Goal: Return matching landmarks. Challenge: Visual similarity between buildings across the globe and handling nocturnal vs diurnal photos of the same site.
competitions.solution_summary: Ensemble of Vision Transformers with Cosine Similarity search. 1st place utilized an ensemble of DeiT and ConvNeXt backbones trained with ArcFace loss. They implemented 'Style-Invariant' augmentation where they synthesized night-time versions of day-time photos to force the model to focus on geometry rather than lighting. They used 'Database Augmentation' (DBA).

competitions.title: Google Landmark Recognition 2023
competitions.prompt: Identify world landmarks in images across 100,000+ classes. Data: 4M images with high label noise. Goal: Predict landmark ID. Challenge: Extreme class cardinality and the long-tail distribution where thousands of classes have only 1-2 examples.
competitions.solution_summary: Sub-center ArcFace with Dynamic Margin Scaling. 1st place utilized an ensemble of EfficientNet-B7 and ConvNeXt-Large. They implemented 'Dynamic Margin Scaling' where the ArcFace margin was increased for rare classes to improve separation. They used 'Pseudo-labeling' to use a large pool of unlabeled travel photos from the internet.

competitions.title: Google Landmark Recognition 2024
competitions.prompt: Recognize world landmarks from a globally diverse dataset of 5M+ images. Data: High-resolution images from travel blogs and citizen science. Goal: Predict landmark ID. Challenge: Handling the visual shift between professional travel photos and low-quality mobile uploads.
competitions.solution_summary: Ensemble of Foundation Vision-Language Models. 1st place utilized a CLIP-style visual backbone fine-tuned for landmark retrieval. They implemented 'Domain-Adversarial training' where the model was forced to produce identical features for professional and mobile photos of the same site. They used 'Balanced Sampling' to handle the massive class imbalance.
